price_tables.label: Gateway illustrative table
price_tables.description: The dated, illustrative three-tier table of semantic-cache-gateway (first model of each tier). Round numbers in the range public price lists use for small, mid-size and frontier models; not a quote from any provider.

price_tables.label: Gateway narrow table
price_tables.description: The gateway benchmark's second table, where the large tier costs only about 4x the small tier on output. It shows how much of any routing saving is the price gap rather than the router.

price_tables.label: Trajectory-gate flat table
price_tables.description: The single illustrative price of a small hosted model used by trajectory-eval-gate's example agent. Every tier costs the same, so routing has no effect under this table.

price_tables.label: Scenario: premium large tier
price_tables.description: HYPOTHETICAL, defined in this repository only. The gateway's illustrative small and medium prices with a large tier five times more expensive (15/75), standing in for a reasoning-class model. It is a stress test of how much each task depends on its large-tier calls, not a quote.

task.title: Support answer
task.summary: One answer through the gateway, the proxy, memory recall, agentic RAG and the context assembler.
notes: The agentic RAG generator calls the model at temperature 0.1 and the gateway caches only requests at or below cache.max_temperature (0.0 by default), so as composed today the cache never serves this task. The 'cache aligned' scenario assumes the generator is moved to temperature 0.
Routing shares are the gateway's measured routing of its synthetic support workload, applied to these prompts by assumption.

task.title: Coding task (3 reviewers @ 0.8)
task.summary: A programming task through the supervisor, researcher, coder, sandboxed executor and reviewers.
notes: Calls and payload tokens are the swarm's offline measurements with simulated agent competence; the success rate is measured by running the accepted code against hidden tests.
Swarm agents call models at temperature 0.2 and every task is different, so no cache hit is assumed.

task.title: Research workflow (durable, crash p=0)
task.summary: Plan, gather sources (GraphRAG local search, no LLM offline), draft, wait for approval, publish once.

latency.label: one durable step (SQLite WAL, checkpoint every transition)

notes: The crash model assumes every step attempt crashes independently with the same probability and that a crash wastes the tokens of the interrupted attempt.
In the chaos benchmark, 200 kills over 756 runs caused 89 re-run attempts and no completed step ran twice.

task.title: Pull-request gate (offline judge)
task.summary: Re-run the agent on every eval case, grade each run against its golden DAG, compare with the baseline.
notes: Eval runs must bypass the response cache: a temperature-0 cache would replay the baseline and hide both regressions and flakiness.
Token counts are the scripted travel-desk agent's simulated usage, not a live model's.

assumptions.rationale: Prompt budget for one support answer: the smallest budget at which the context assembler kept every planted fact in its benchmark (measurement assembler.retention_at_3072).
Mean answer length. The agentic RAG generator caps answers at max_tokens=500 (generate.py); half of the cap is assumed.
An LLM query rewrite sees the question, the grader's diagnosis and an instruction block; no repository measures it.
A few rewritten queries returned as JSON.
With a key, consolidation runs an LLM summary and an LLM fact extraction; one consolidation per session is assumed.
Instructions and output schema around the flushed turns of a consolidation call.
A short summary or a JSON list of facts.
Role instructions plus the JSON schema of the expected artifact, which the offline payload estimate leaves out. Order of magnitude implied by agents/prompts.py, not measured.
The swarm reports request + reply tokens as one number; replies (code, votes) are assumed to be 35% of it.
Brief, instructions and the plan schema.
Draft prompt filled to the largest budget of the context assembler's sweep (8,192), where its fact retention is 100%.
The travel-desk suite has five cases (trajectory-eval-gate benchmark setup).
Runs per case for each pull request, as in the trajectory-eval-gate benchmark (benchmark.json /setup/candidate_run_set).
Baseline runs per case, as in the trajectory-eval-gate benchmark.
The baseline is re-recorded once every 20 merged pull requests, so its cost is spread over 20.
